Title: Free Up Space From Old Windows Update Files
Author: Core Lord
Data:
# **⚡ Quick Method — Disk Cleanup**
**The easiest and safest way to remove old Windows Update files without using CMD or PowerShell.**
1. Press Win + R 2. Type cleanmgr and press Enter 3. Select your C: drive 4. Click Clean up system files 5. Select C: again 6. Enable the cleanup options below 7. Recommended options: ``` • Windows Update Cleanup • Previous Windows Installations • Delivery Optimization Files ``` > Windows Update Cleanup can often free between 3 GB and 15 GB. --- # 🛠 DISM Cleanup Commands Use DISM to remove superseded and outdated update components. ### Standard Cleanup **CMD / PowerShell (Admin)** `Dism.exe /Online /Cleanup-Image /StartComponentCleanup` ### Aggressive Cleanup **CMD / PowerShell (Admin)** `Dism.exe /Online /Cleanup-Image /StartComponentCleanup /ResetBase` > Using `/ResetBase` prevents uninstalling current Windows updates later. Only use it if your system is stable. --- # 🧹 Clear Windows Update Cache This removes downloaded update installer files from the Windows Update cache. Windows will automatically recreate them if needed. **CMD (Admin)** ``` net stop wuauserv net stop bits rd /s /q %windir%\SoftwareDistribution\Download net start wuauserv net start bits ``` > The SoftwareDistribution\Download folder stores temporary Windows Update installation files. --- # 📦 Clear Delivery Optimization Cache Remove cached update-sharing files downloaded from or shared with other PCs. **CMD (Admin)** `del /f /s /q %windir%\ServiceProfiles\NetworkService\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Windows\DeliveryOptimization\Cache\*` --- # 💾 Estimated Space Recovery | Cleanup Type | Estimated Space | | -------- | -------- | | Windows Update Cleanup | 500 MB – 15 GB | | SoftwareDistribution Cache | 100 MB – 5 GB | | Delivery Optimization Cache | 0 – 10 GB | --- # 🚫 Do Not Delete These Manually ``` Avoid manually deleting: • C:\Windows\WinSxS • C:\Windows\Installer Removing files directly from these folders can break Windows or installed applications. ``` --- # ✅ Safe Cleanup Rule If your PC has been running normally for at least 7 days after the latest Windows update, it is generally safe to remove old update files and cleanup caches.
